title: 1951 AHSME Problem 36
statement: Which of the following methods of proving a geometric figure a locus is not correct?

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text:
Every point on the locus satisfies the conditions and every
point not on the locus does not satisfy the conditions.

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
Every point not satisfying the conditions is
not on the locus and every point on the locus does satisfy the
conditions.

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
Every point satisfying the conditions is on the locus and every
point on the locus satisfies the conditions.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
Every point not on the locus does not satisfy the conditions
and every point not satisfying the conditions is not on the
locus.

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
Every point satisfying the conditions is on the locus and every
point not satisfying the conditions is not on the locus.

solutions.text:
Let \(L\) mean “on the locus” and \(C\) mean “satisfies the conditions.” A complete proof needs both \(L\Rightarrow C\) and \(C\Rightarrow L.\) Choice B states \(\neg C\Rightarrow\neg L,\) which is merely the contrapositive of \(L\Rightarrow C,\) and then repeats \(L\Rightarrow C.\) It never proves \(C\Rightarrow L.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: A locus proof needs both implications between “on the locus” and “satisfies the conditions”
Use contrapositives to see whether each choice establishes both directions
